title: Periodic trends: predict, then say what measures them
promptMarkdown:
Write this without the notes open (under 350 words), then compare with lecture 8 pages 2–4.

1. Rank Na, Mg, K and Cl by atomic radius (largest first) and by first ionisation energy (lowest first). Give a one-line reason for each ranking in terms of the shell number $n$ and the effective nuclear charge.
2. Explain the two irregularities in the second period: why the first ionisation energy of B is below that of Be, and why that of O is below that of N.
3. Which experiment measures ionisation energies directly, and what observation in it would contradict your ranking in part 1?
4. Using the sign convention of lecture 8 ($\text{EA} = -\Delta E$ for $\ce{X(g) + e- -> X-(g)}$), explain why chlorine has a large positive electron affinity and neon an unfavourable one.
hintLadder: Across a period $n$ is fixed and $Z$ grows; down a group $n$ grows. Decide which effect dominates in each direction.
Write the configurations of Be, B, N and O and look at which subshell the outermost electron occupies and whether it is paired.
Photoelectron spectroscopy measures electron kinetic energies for a known photon energy; the binding energy is the difference.

deterministicChecks.description: asserting that ionisation energy increases down a group or that atomic radius increases across a period

criteria.criterion: Radius K > Na > Mg > Cl and IE K < Na < Mg < Cl, each with the n / effective-nuclear-charge reason.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Rankings right, reasons thin or one slip.

criteria.criterion: B below Be because the 2p electron is higher in energy and better shielded than 2s; O below N because the fourth 2p electron pairs and repulsion lowers its binding.

Photoelectron spectroscopy named, with the contradicting observation stated (for example Mg's outermost peak at higher kinetic energy than Na's at the same photon energy would mean a lower IE for Mg).

levels.label: met
levels.description: Experiment and a concrete contradicting observation.

criteria.criterion: Cl releases energy on gaining an electron that completes the 3p subshell (EA positive in this convention); Ne's added electron would open a new shell, so energy is required.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Both, with the sign convention respected.

checkExamples.label: correct explanation
checkExamples.text: Radius: K > Na > Mg > Cl, since K has the largest n and across period 3 the rising Z pulls electrons in at fixed n. IE: K < Na < Mg < Cl, for the same reasons in reverse: ionization energy decreases down a group and increases across a period. B is below Be because its outer electron is in 2p, higher than 2s; O is below N because the fourth 2p electron must pair. Photoelectron spectroscopy measures the kinetic energies of electrons ejected by X-rays of known energy; if the outermost peak of Mg appeared at a higher kinetic energy than that of Na, Mg's IE would be lower and my ranking wrong. Cl gains an electron into a nearly full 3p subshell and releases energy (EA > 0); Ne would have to start a new shell, so energy is required.

checkExamples.label: reversed group trend
checkExamples.text: Ionization energy increases down a group because there are more protons, so K has the highest ionization energy of the four.
